provenance.v1_1_correction: v1.0 aggregated by tier alone. The full_corpus cell and the small cell came from two different pipelines -- a bond-head reconstruction of REAL tmQM geometries versus free generation -- so v1.0's 'training scale' reading compared two pipelines.
provenance.v1_2_correction: pools are deduplicated on file content (sha256), because two directories holding the same molecules were counted twice and doubled the full-corpus tier.
provenance.v1_3_correction: sha256 alone stopped working once the full run resumed to 18 epochs: the 4-epoch partial is then a strict prefix, not a copy. A pool whose (epoch, smiles) rows are a subset of a kept pool's is now dropped as a prefix.
provenance.v1_4_pool_kind: the pool-kind rule has ONE owner: molmetal/scripts/cfm_pool_kind.py.  The mixed by_tier cell is replaced by the kind-separated by_tier_by_kind view; by_tier itself is only replaced under CFM_POOL_KIND_STRICT=1.
provenance.v1_5_pool_kind: the pool kind is decided by CONTENT, not by the header.  MEASURED: cfm_fullcorpus_2026_10_10 has sanitized == 0 on 66/66 rows and an empty metal_z on 66/66 -> FREE GENERATION (the ODE path); cfm_fullcorpus_b64_2026_10_11 (40 rows) and cfm_objective_terms_2026_10_11 (43 rows) have sanitized == 1 and a populated metal_z on every row -> RECONSTRUCTION.  A pool whose signals disagree is UNKNOWN and is never pooled into a kind.
provenance.v1_6_cohort_owner: the cohort (n_train / n_val) has ONE owner: the census's own ts-attested resolution (run.n_train / run.n_val with its cohort_source), with molmetal/scripts/cfm_cohort_recovery.py::recover_cohort as the fallback.  The run's own per_epoch_metrics.json is written ONCE at the END of training to a FIXED path, so a later run launched into the same --out-dir overwrites it; that clobbered file can no longer win.  MEASURED: cfm_fullcorpus_2026_10_10's file reads n_train=64 / n_val=32 (a 1-epoch CPU smoke) while the run of record's cohort is 26715/192 (census, run_log:ts_matched).
provenance.v1_6_epoch_aligned_gen_validity: the gen_validity published on a pool row is the resolved POPULATION's value AT THE POOL'S OWN LAST EPOCH -- the epoch whose molecules the pool contains -- taken from the AGGREGATE row (the one carrying gen_validity_n), never from the per-seed rows and never from another epoch.  The SA / QED on the same row describe that epoch, so a validity from another epoch describes a different model.  The population is the RUN OF RECORD, segmented by the census's own _event_segments / _population_decision; a run the census does not carry falls back to the segment that CONTAINS the pool's epoch.  MEASURED: cfm_fullcorpus_2026_10_10's pool is epoch 10 and its run of record's epoch-10 aggregate is 0.3255208333333333 (n=768); the value the old 'last logged row' rule published was the epoch-0 row of a LATER 1-epoch CPU smoke that wrote into the same directory (0.9140625, n=128).
provenance.v1_6_pool_own_draw: the pool's OWN draw (how many of its attempts yielded a molecule) is published SEPARATELY, in gen_validity_pool, with its own source string, so it can never be read as the run of record's gen_validity.  MEASURED: cfm_fullcorpus_2026_10_10 holds the 66 survivors of 192 attempts (66/192 = 0.34375); the free-generation panel records the same draw and rounds it to 0.344.

selection_gap.note: cfm_sa_guided.json scores the generator's pools (2,396 molecules from three runs with n_train 26715/256/256) and, separately, the two full-corpus RECONSTRUCTION pools in their own block -- the two are never pooled into one rate.

verdict.reading: Only pools from the same pipeline are comparable: a bond-head reconstruction of a real tmQM geometry inherits real chemistry, so its SA score is not generator quality. A full-corpus free-generation pool exists (14846 molecules, SA<=4.5 = 0.0040 [0.0031, 0.0052]). The small tier (n_train < 1024) scores 0.0069 [0.0042, 0.0111], so scaling to the full corpus is not better on this gate. gen_validity is the one metric both scales compute through the same path, and it does not improve with scale on the runs that have it.
